proposedOverrides.summary: Localized Pre-Roman Iron Age evidence with the atlas label and geometry defects disclosed.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact id is germanic-tribes, display name Germanic tribes, circa 400 to 323 BCE; Germanic is treated as a later analytical umbrella, not one self-named people, state, language, ethnicity, or uniform culture.
The unrelated-looking indexed alias Mgadha is disclosed as a data defect and never treated as an ancient synonym.

The sole polygon has one component and 253 positions; among thirty-five fixed probes it contains only Gothenburg, Oslo, and Uppsala while excluding Denmark, Jastorf, Tollund, Hjortspring, and Stockholm.
At 400 BCE most continental probes are assigned to the hallstatt-culture layer, while the target shares one encoded arc with saami; neither construction is treated as a real cultural border.
Jastorf and Pre-Roman Iron Age are archaeological categories. Claims keep direct finds, laboratory measurements, experiments, interpretive models, and later comparisons distinct.

No contemporaneous written-language sample is securely attributable; later runes, reconstructed Proto-Germanic forms, Pytheas fragments, and Roman ethnonyms are explicitly excluded as local text samples.
The 323 BCE disappearance is an atlas seam, not a fall, conquest, migration, language replacement, or extinction event; continuity is explicit and no successor is invented.
